utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry we're late in starting. The fault was mine. I forgot that we had an initial appearance in another case which we had to deal with first. But we'll go on. Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, we can continue. To start off today, I have a set of questions related to Mr. Kordic. You said that Mr. Kordic was one of the party leaders in the Vatrostalna company. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was common knowledge, as far as I know, that he worked in the Vatrostalna company, that he was a journalist, and at one point he was a party leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I didn't ask you what his job was in Vatrostalna. You emphasised that he was a party leader. Tell the Trial Chamber, in concrete terms, what he actually was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think he was the secretary of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Are you certain that he was that at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think he was, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you're not quite sure, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't work in Vatrostalna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Although you didn't work in Vatrostalna, as you say, you say that Mr. Kordic very regularly performed his work duties without making any mistakes, without a single mistake, I believe you said. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was common knowledge to all of us in town, that he was a conscientious young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Apart from that general answer of it being common knowledge, do you know any of his work duties that he performed, any concrete work duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It's not my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know what assignments and tasks he had. But that he did carry them out as they should have been, I do know that, because that was common knowledge, as I say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you said that Mr. Dario Kordic was the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Can you tell us what the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in fact was when it was established? What was it at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: For us Muslims, it was a catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, at the time when the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was set up, who was the aggressor in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Yugoslav army, aided and abetted by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where do you draw the conclusion from that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, when it was formed, was a catastrophe for the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because we all had to come under the command of the HVO and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know when the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know the year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps that is not essential for me, personally, but it was in 1992 sometime. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: 1992, you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps even before that. But in 1992, in Tomislavgrad, some events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We'll go back to that later. You said that as the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Kordic replaced Mr. Boban, and you said that he was quite obviously in charge of the Lasva Valley. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's quite simple. Mr. Kordic was in Busovaca and he operated first in Busovaca, and the event happened, what happened, and then it continued throughout the Lasva Valley. For us Muslims and for me, that was sufficient proof that Dario Kordic was the sole person in command of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So that is your conclusion, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is my conclusion and the conclusion of all the Muslims in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what do you imply when you say "the Lasva Valley"? What municipalities are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there's Busovaca, which does not tend towards Lasva. Vitez, Travnik, Novi Travnik, in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what functions did Mr. Kordic have in the Lasva Valley as a deputy for Mr. Boban? Do you know what tasks he had, what concrete assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not, but we all know. Even the smallest children in Busovaca knew that Dario Kordic was the number one in command and that everything was under his command, political, military, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I am asking you, as you're saying so with such assurance that he was a commander, the commander, could you tell us what assignments he had, without generally giving us answers and telling us what we all know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was there, sir, and I lived through it all, I experienced it. Everything that happened there happened under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you haven't got any concrete examples as to what his job was as the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the political onslaught in Tomislavgrad, as you said. Tell us when that onslaught took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was sometime in 1992. I don't know exactly, I have lost count of the dates, but television and the radio spoke a great deal about those events. That is quite certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. If you can't tell us the time and date, what you said was essential, and you said that at that meeting held in Tomislavgrad, I think that you said that Kljujic ^ was taken off and that Boban was put in his place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What was the post that Mr. Boban occupied when he came there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Boban performed the function at that time -- he was in charge of everything. He was in charge of the entire HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. But what was his post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, probably he was the president or whatever it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: President of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The HDZ, you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the military, political, and I don't know how to put it, put all that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you claim, if I understood you correctly, that Mr. Mate Boban replaced Mr. Kljujic ^ as president of the HDZ; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you don't know exactly when Mr. Boban became president of the HDZ of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Professor/Dr. Brkic, Miljenko Brkic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That name doesn't seem to ring a bell at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, let me remind you. Mr. Brkic was the president of the HDZ in the period after, that is to say, in between Mr. Kljujic ^ and Mr. Boban in the course of 1992. You didn't know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You didn't know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You say you've never heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I have heard of him, but it doesn't ring a bell. And even if it was the case, it was only on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you got any concrete arguments to put forward to support your conclusion that this was only on paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could say that the commands came down from Boban to Kordic and Kordic put them into practice in Busovaca, and later on did so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us how you know this. How do you know that Mr. Kordic received a single order or whatever from Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, everybody knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking for a concrete example. Let's see what you know in concrete terms; not "we" but you, what you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, if we look at some things which took place in Busovaca, which is where ethnic cleansing in fact started, as far as I know, no Muslims in town gave any reason for this kind of thing to happen, for them to be expelled, for houses to be stormed and looted, and so on and everything else that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, I have to interrupt you, although this isn't very good for the interpreters, but I would like to ask you for a concrete answer to save time. Can you give us any concrete order or any instructions that Mr. Kordic received from Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, sir, I did not have an insight into that, nor was that possible, nor could any of the Muslims have had any insight into that. But the acts that were performed testify sufficiently to where everything came from and originated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So as far as I understand it, that is only your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not only my conclusion but it is the conclusion of all the Muslims in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you know when Mr. Kordic became the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the dates. I can't tell you any dates now, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know when Mr. Kordic became the vice-president of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the dates of all those events and all the dates and everything that took place in the HDZ and when it occurred, but it is common knowledge and that the dates are common knowledge as well. You have to ask, because it is all common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, a "no" would be a sufficient answer. I just want to see what you know and what you don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any chronology of the events, I didn't record them, and even if I did have some notebooks, they were all burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that Mr. Kljujic ^ was for a multi-ethnic Bosnia-Herzegovina. How do you know that? What does that mean, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, what it means, it means that he was in favour of coexistence, and all of us Muslims respected him highly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know this personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What are your sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, via the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You also claim that, on the other hand, Mr. Boban and Mr. Kordic were, as you said, hard-liners. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, had they not been hard-liners, what happened would not have happened. I would be in my own house now. I wouldn't have experienced the camps. I wouldn't have been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you mean to say there would have been no war then? That is the gist of your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, as we have mentioned the HDZ at a high level, you spoke about the organisation of the HDZ or, rather, the Croatian authorities in the region of Busovaca, and you mentioned Dr. Franc, who was on the HDZ list for the elections. You say that he was replaced from his post. What post did he hold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, when the elections were held, this was a joint list, and Dr. Franc was on it as head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The joint HDZ list and SDA, if I remember correctly, in order to overthrow the existing powers that be in Communist. Dr. Franc was the leader, and thanks to that very fact that Dr. Franc headed the list, the coalition won the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I didn't understand what position he held when he was replaced.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: If he was the head leader of the list and if he got the majority vote, then he probably had the top function in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So that is your conclusion, is it, that he held the top post, regardless of his age and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, if he was on the list, then he should have performed those tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to quarrel, but I see that this is your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it's not my conclusion. Those are the facts as they stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know what else he was? For example, do you know the structure of the HDZ for the Busovaca municipality in 1991/'92?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who the first president of the HDZ was, for example, in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who the second president of the HDZ in Busovaca was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I cannot enumerate that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't know, then, who the presidents and vice-presidents were of the HDZ in Busovaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know something more about the organisation of the HDZ in the Busovaca municipality or any more details about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I wasn't that interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When we speak about Mr. Kordic, you said that Mr. Kordic was involved in everything, and that's why I'm asking you. Do you know, for example, when the HDZ of Busovaca was ranked, whether he had any position, performed any function at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but I do know that at the founding meeting, he was the conferencier of the HDZ in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, that's not surprising, because he's a journalist by vocation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. So you don't know his functions. We don't want to tire the Trial Chamber anymore.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who did what, but that everything revolved around Dario Kordic later on, that is something I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is your general answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's not my answer, it is the answer of the whole Muslim population of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. J, let us proceed. You said that Mr. Kordic wore a uniform. Tell us, please, do you know when he started wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that I saw him for the first time in uniform when planes were shelling Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The first or second shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Really, whether it was the first or not, I don't think that is important, I can't remember, but that is when I saw him for the first time in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Kordic wore a uniform, that he was a colonel, and that he wore the rank insignia on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that that is what I said. I just said that he had the rank of colonel. Who gave him that rank, I don't know. That he had the rank of colonel and that that was how he was introduced on the media and everywhere else, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that, on page 65, on the 39th day of the hearing, I think it was Thursday -- my English is not too good, but I can see here that it says that he wore rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Could I ask my colleague to look at it, page 65, lines 13 to 16 of the transcript. So my colleague is confirming that I'm right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what these markings of the rank looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't say that I saw him wearing rank. But that he had the rank of colonel and that he was introduced as a colonel, that is what I did say regarding Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So this is not correct, what I found on the transcript as a record of your testimony on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that I saw his rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the date from when he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you must ask him that, when he acquired the rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But could you tell us roughly in time? Was it the beginning of '92, the middle, the end, or 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, and I don't think it is very important. The important thing is that he had this rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But how do you know that, by what? Did you see any document about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Who could have seen any document among the Muslims or had any access to anything at all? It's an absurd question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that in view of the uniform he wore, that he was no longer a politician, that he was a military man, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I think that yesterday I quoted from your statement that you gave in January 1997, when you said that Mr. Tihomir Blaskic was a professional soldier, and that sentence has an addition to it, and that is, "while Mr. Dario Kordic was something else." So what was he, a soldier or a politician, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Dario Kordic combined all of that together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean the military and the political?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the military and the political.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When we were speaking a moment ago about the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, you said at the previous hearing that the aim was to annex it to the Republic of Croatia, that that was the aim of the Croatian Community. When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You know that there was a referendum in Bosnia-Herzegovina for its independence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you also know that the Croats voted for the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, at the last minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you also know that in Busovaca, the town of Busovaca, a list was signed in favour of the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So when you claim that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna wanted to join up with Croatia, do you mean at the beginning, before the referendum, or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sir, it is common knowledge that that was the main and principal goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you have any concrete evidence of that, any particular act, any specific act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could mention an example. When I was released from prison, from the camp, in a conversation with Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you already told us that. But apart from that. We're talking about Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No one else would have known any such thing if he hadn't heard it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, you said that it is common knowledge in Busovaca that Mr. Kordic went to Grude frequently to attend meetings with Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he did, under an armed escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: How do you personally know that, Mr. J?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had occasion to see that convoy, consisting of two or three vehicles, passing by and coming back two or three days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about departures from Busovaca. I'm asking you how do you know that Mr. Kordic was in Grude with Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Where else could he go?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, it is just your conclusion that he went frequently to see Mr. Boban in Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you have nothing more to tell us, from your personal experience, except for saying "logical"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Naumovski, we've covered this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour. As I have been told to proceed, I will have to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In this context, you also said that various cars with license plates from other towns would come to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So could you please tell us about when this occurred, if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Not dates, but roughly. A part of which year, which month, something closer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps in the autumn of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, around about then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that you saw license plates of Vitez, Novi Travnik, Kiseljak, and that you concluded on that basis that those vehicles were coming from different parts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not wish to waste any time, but yesterday I showed you the travel permit signed by Mr. Djidic, as a commander of the Territorial Defence of the Vitez municipality, and a new license plate for the whole region is mentioned, and this is the end of '92, and the town mentioned is Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but you could still know, by the numbers, which municipality people came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So not by the letters but by the numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Both by the numbers and by the letters that figured on the license plate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me ask you directly. Do you know when those license plates were changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't exactly, but my Golf had the license plate Z945, and this was a Busovaca license plate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we're talking about new license plates with the Travnik indication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really can't remember when this was introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that people were coming to visit Mr. Kordic. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because they went in the direction of Tisovac, and up there, there was nothing else but Kordic's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who else was with Mr. Kordic, who worked there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't know a single other name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: All the other names were insignificant for us, more or less, because they were simply carrying out orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that is your conclusion, the same general conclusion that you are making?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not mine, but of the entire Muslim population in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mention was made here of certain Golf cars. I don't consider this story important, but since you linked it to Mr. Kordic, I have to ask you something about it. Do you have any piece of evidence that Mr. Kordic had anything to do with the distribution of those Golf cars, or anything at all in connection with those cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that he knew nothing about it? If those Golf cars were driven off to Tisovac, of course he knew everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Are you sure that they ended up in Tisovac, or rather from where were you watching people passing towards Tisovac? I assume from your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But I could have also been watching from my brother-in-law's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But all this is before the village of Ravan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And the village of Ravan, you said, is a Croatian village? I mean, inhabitants living there. Well, how do you know those vehicles didn't end up there? Perhaps there was an office there dealing with them, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly, but still, this was under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that is your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It is not my conclusion. That village was inhabited exclusively by Croats, as you said. There were probably warehouses there, and I don't know what else, so that Mr. Kordic was in charge of all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you have any record, any direct proof of what you are saying, any detail that would corroborate this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, for instance, a great deal of arms was driven off there, from the direction of Kaonik, in military trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You saw that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Trucks, fully loaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: With what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: With boxes, typical boxes carrying rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you didn't see what was in those boxes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that would be a bit too much. Who do you think would let me have a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: How would it be possible for anyone to approach and examine what's inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mentioning the village of Ravan, you referred to a speech which allegedly Mr. Kordic made there in 1992. Will you please tell us, which part of 1992? Could you fix that event in time a little closer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I apologise. I mentioned that in passing, and I received this information from somebody else, and that is why I mentioned it. This person witnessed the speech, and he could directly confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When was this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I really can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When did you hear about those events, when you don't know when they actually took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe two or three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So two or three years ago, you heard that Mr. Kordic allegedly said something in the village of Ravan in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know in connection with what? What was taking place in that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really wouldn't like to go into that, because I don't know much about it, but there is a person [Realtime transcript read in error "American"] who is willing to come and tell you about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you to tell Their Honours who told you about that event.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You can't tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't tell you the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So all you know about it, you know it from what you were told by this man, and who told you this quite recently, you said, two years ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let us say so, yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, were you aware of that event in January 1997 when you spoke to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you know about it when you made your statement in another case before this Court, in the Aleksovski case, on the 2nd of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me put it differently. Could you be more precise as to when you learned about this alleged speech in the village of Ravan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: How can I know? I really can't give you a concrete answer, but the person who was present -- and he's willing to come and tell you about it. That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I think there was a typographical -- a translation error.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Pardon me. Back at line -- the time -- 15.07.37, a reference to -- this person was described as an American, and I think the witness's statement was there was a man. I don't think there was any testimony that this person was an American, just so the record is clear. If the witness wants to clarify that -- excuse me; if Mr. Naumovski would like to clarify that by further --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: He said "man." He said "man." That is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) He didn't want to tell us who this man is. He probably has his own reasons. But how, then, can he explain it to us if we don't know who it is? Because Mr. Kordic never said that. But let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, on a number of occasions, and maybe dozens of times, you said that Mr. Kordic was the number one in Busovaca, that he had absolute control over the police and the army and so on, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he controlled everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you know who was the head of the civilian police in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who was the head of the civilian police in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that there was Nikica Petrovic, Vlado Cosic, and I don't know who else and what position they held exactly, but I knew that they were among the most important people in the police. That I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We'll come later to the gentleman called Cosic, but I was asking you about the civilian police. Do you know that there was a civilian and a military police in Busovaca throughout the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was all one police. What are you talking about, civilian and military?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So according to you, there's no distinction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not in that period of time, because the police consisted exclusively of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But we're saying now, was there civilian and military, or was it all one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: For us it was all one. We had a bad time whoever it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Claiming that Mr. Kordic was number 1, you said on a number of occasions that this was -- logic itself led to that conclusion, that Mr. Kordic was number 1. So if I can put it that way, it is what you would consider a logical conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, let's say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But tell me, please, did you personally see a single document issued by Mr. Kordic, for instance, to the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But who among the Muslims could have seen any document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But, Mr. J, we have to support your conclusions with something apart from you just saying, in general terms, he was number 1. Did you see any order to a military unit signed by Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But that was impossible. Even in theory, no one could have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: Did he ever sign such an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ask him. No Muslim could have got anywhere close to any such things, never mind actually seeing or having access to such documents. It's out of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One moment. Witness J, we might get on more quickly if you just said "Yes" or "No" to questions of that sort. Mr. Naumovski, we must finish this witness today, so would you draw your cross-examination to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I promised Your Honour, I will do my very best, but I really do have a lot of questions because the witness covered great deal of ground, and I beg you for understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you were talking about the police, do you remember, did they wear different kinds of uniforms? For instance, did they have blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No? Thank you. Yesterday -- let us make a step forward, to speed things up -- you were saying, when you were in Kaonik and were taken to dig somewhere, you said that you spoke to two soldiers, Gardanjski and Josip Condra, and they told that you they would talk to Mr. Kordic about the conditions in the camp, in the prison and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was in Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who were they, these soldiers? Were they ordinary soldiers or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms, I'm sure of that, but whether they were ordinary soldiers, obviously not, because they were carrying out some kind of control. They were not guards, they were not on the front, they were not guarding us. They were there carrying out some sort of inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know which unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know which brigade they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the name, but all of them belonged to one brigade in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you know that in January, 1993, there was an HVO brigade formed in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In January '93?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, when these things that you told us about were happening.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That happened in the camp, this particular incident, on the 6th of February, at Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but we are talking about this period, January/February. Do you know that there was an HVO brigade in Busovaca then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably, yes. When exactly it was formed, I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Never mind. That was not my question. My question is, who was the commander of the HVO brigade in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you don't know any member of the command of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: What exact positions those individuals had, I really don't know, but it wasn't important for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't know a single name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I couldn't really recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, I think it was yesterday, or before that, you spoke about the circumstances under which your house was burnt. You told us yesterday that your brother-in-law -- that is, your wife's brother -- that in front of your house, a yellow car was seen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: White.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, white. Maybe I made a mistake. Did he tell you what the license plates were on that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did he tell you the make of the car, the model?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember him telling me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But how, then, is that car linked to Mr. Kordic's brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because he personally knew that that was his car, and that house is only 10 metres away from mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But there are hundreds of white cars all over, including Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But not in those days. There weren't any cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know the name of Mr. Kordic's brother at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it's Darko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But it's not Darko; that's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But that doesn't matter. His name isn't important. Names didn't really mean much in Busovaca. We knew each other very well without that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, there's a problem distinguishing between question and answer, so can you allow a pause, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour. I have tried to prevent that, but I'll take more care.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So I have made the mistake that I asked you to avoid. So your brother-in-law told you that this car had been seen, but did he tell you who he saw in person in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Kordic's brother and Atso (phoen).

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Aleksandar Ruzic, you mean? But you were not so explicit the last time. You said that Kordic's brother's car was seen rather than Kordic's brother. There's a difference there, you know. There's a difference. Even in these questions, in the outline prepared by the Prosecutor, I think that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you claim that your brother-in-law told you that he was there, I mean Dario's brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, you have given several statements to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal; I assume you remember that. And you have already testified in this Court, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You made a statement on the 18th of February, 1992 (sic), and the 8th of September, 1995, so that is one and the same statement, only it has two dates. Both are in '95. On page 6 of this statement, it says: "My house was burned down by Darko Kordic, Aleksandar Ruzic, known as Atso (phoen), and Kulic. His car was seen next to my car when they were torching my house." Now comes the part why I'm asking you this. You said, "I heard that when I saw some Croats here in Zenica."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is true, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But there's no mention of your brother-in-law in this story, when you talked to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably later on he told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: My colleague has found the question, question Number 68 in the Prosecutor's outline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, I think we've spent enough time on this issue. You've made your point about it, and you may have ground to cover, but you can really do it more quickly, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours. Just a couple of questions more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, I have just read to you quite a different tale, that you learnt from some people in Zenica what had happened to your house when you went to Zenica, rather than from your brother-in-law, as you told Their Honours here in court. Which is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention that ever before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't want to involve him in it, and that is the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What is your brother-in-law's name, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether that is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, it's a matter for us to decide whether it's important. But Mr. Naumovski, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, let us proceed. You spoke yesterday about an event that took place when you returned from Putis, when you were in Kaonik, and you were on a bridge when a U.N. vehicle appeared and a female reporter asked a soldier something. Do you remember that portion of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: How many people were there on the bridge, soldiers and those of you from the Kaonik prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 20. About 20. There were about 20 of us prisoners and a few guards who were escorting us to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know which unit they belonged to, those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, and what we learnt that night, they were the Vitez people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you said that the woman asked one of them something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What language did she put her question in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In our language.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: She spoke our language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What did she ask him, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: She asked him where he was taking the people and what was going on, where the people were going, why he was taking them off. And his answer was, "Leave me alone. Go and ask Dario Kordic. I don't know, because I was brought here too."

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So that soldier, the soldier that we said was from Vitez, had no rank insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't see any, no. I don't think he did have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So as a soldier from Vitez, he answered the reporter and told her what you just said; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now a few more words about the events concerning your stay in Kaonik. You said that Mr. Aleksovski, as the commander, said that he needed a permit, a certificate to be signed by either Mr. Kordic or Mr. Sliskovic to release anybody from the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it wasn't a permit; it was -- they were people that were to go out digging, and they had to have a paper allowing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So a list, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, sir, not as a list. Quite simply, we were distributed into work platoons, and when requested from a particular department, 30 people were asked for digging purposes, Aleksovski did not allow this because he told the man, when he gave him the piece of paper -- I don't know what was written on the paper, but he said that Mr. Kordic or Sliskovic had not signed the paper and that he could not let the men go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you see that particular paper, the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was four or five metres away. I just saw a piece of paper. What was written on it, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you were standing at that distance, but you heard the words they uttered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Some 20 of us were lined up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you ever see, while you were in Kaonik, a document, a paper, signed by Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we were prisoners, for heaven's sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Kordic in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that Mr. Kordic controlled the radio and television in Busovaca. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there was just the Croatian programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you in the context of Mr. Kordic. You said that Mr. Kordic had control of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think that I told you at least ten times that everything was under his control and baton.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: For what period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Will you give us the beginning and end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let us say from May 1992 to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, you mentioned that on several occasions that Mr. Kordic was the main commander and that everybody took their orders from him. But in concrete terms, you never saw a single order issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've asked that question on a number of occasions. We don't need to go over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: If you agree, Mr. J, let us now move on to January 1993 and the events that took place from the 20th onwards. Would you please tell us where you were after you left your house; that is to say, between the 22nd and 25th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Any kind of fortification for defence purposes or attack purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, you have told us some data about some Muslims who were, in fact, killed in January, in the course of the 25th of January 1993, but I have a piece of information whereby those were practically all soldiers. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Kadica Strana, according to my information, had several -- in the military sense of the word, several prepared positions, military positions. The first position was in the first houses by the bridge leading from the centre of town towards Kadica Strana, next to Admir Ekmescic's house. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps it was like that. The young men tried to protect themselves, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So at that position -- perhaps the military term would be a different one, but I'm going to call it a position -- amongst them were Admir Ekmescic, nicknamed Pecin; Adnan Malkic; and Mahir Mekic. Do you know those individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me when I say that they were there during the night between the 24th and 25th of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably they were, because their houses were there, some 10 metres off. Malkic's house is opposite, on the opposite side of the river, and that's where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. That is to say they were there on the night between the 24th and 25th of January but also on the night between the 23rd and 24th of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let us take it that we were all there at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The other combat position, Mr. J, was some 20 metres away from the first position, and there, during the nights that we're discussing, amongst others, were Irfan Beslic, Dzenad Novalic, nicknamed Fosil, you and your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was at my brother's house. That's where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. The third position, in the military sense, was above the fire brigade building facing Kadira Siljka's house, and his nickname was Emso. And among others present there were Sedin Merdan, nicknamed Cero; Nihad Merdan, aka Nina; Irhad Ekmescic, known as Reho; Benjamin Halilovic, nicknamed Benja; Ejnar Begovic; Nedzad Novalic; Asim Sarajlic, nicknamed Sisa, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were all there. That's quite right. We were all gathered there in that particular Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: There was another position above the Bonanza Restaurant, whatever it was called, and present there were Jasmin Sehovic called Rusce (phoen); Hasko Bilac; Tarik Muminovic, nicknamed Mulje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is being put in all of this? Is it being suggested that these men whose names you're reading out were firing or anything of that sort? Surely this can be put more rapidly. Are you suggesting that the Muslims were attacking the Croats or something of that sort?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, we'll go into that in greater detail when we present our defence, but on principle I can say "Yes". I didn't know what the witness would tell me. That is why I collected information on the individuals that were there. If the witness agrees these were combat positions, I can carry on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: You say they were combat positions, whereas I say that we were all gathered in that particular Mahala. Do you think we should have just waited for somebody to attack us? But I ask you, was any bullet fired from that position, as you call it, and did we have any weapons? Nobody fired a single bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Naumovski, I think that we want to proceed quickly, but you must understand that the Trial Chamber has to direct the process in a just and fair way, as you know, and within the limits of the time that we have. I'm waiting for the point in the cross-examination when the Defence will present the Defence case. But we want to know right from now, what is your point; in each cross-examination, what exactly are you trying to show, not to develop ideas whose point we don't see. You must show us what it is you're trying to prove. One should not wait until the end of the Prosecution case to know where you are heading. Tell us where you're going. Otherwise, please go on to another point. Furthermore, I should like to add that according to the Rule, the cross-examination has to be linked to the examination in chief, after all, and it has to refer to a particular point. You can't engage in any point you like. That is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, I understand Your Honour, with all due respect, but this is absolutely in connection with the events of the 25th. That is where everything starts. I'm talking about the 25th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) What the President has asked you and what I am asking you as well is to go directly to the point concerned. You have now described a whole strategy with a large number of individuals, but you must summarise it all in one question within the framework of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well, Your Honour. I'll do my best to summarise as much as possible, and I beg for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, as I have already enumerated all the people, tell me, all those people did not live in Kadica Strana and Kadica Mahala, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So people had come there from other parts of Busovaca; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they were really very far off, that is to say, just across the river. That's how far they were from their homes, individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You say that not a single bullet was fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, not a single one, nor was there any intention of doing that on our part. But we just wanted to gather there and to try to protect ourselves from what was happening. It turned out to be a good thing that we had gathered there, those of us who were left in the Mahala, because the ones that went home in the morning were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you are telling the Trial Chamber that the HVO attacked from 5.00, 5.30, 6.00 in the morning up until 2.00, although you didn't offer the slightest resistance and did not fire a single bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's quite right. It is true that they attacked from half past 5.00 in the morning, that they shot at us with whatever weapons they -- I don't know exactly what weapons they used. But that it was terrible, that is quite true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: A Scorpion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm thinking of all of you, not you personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there was some hunting rifles here and there, or a carbine or something like that. Perhaps there was a PAP-type rifle. But the intention wasn't for us to attack but just to try and defend ourselves as best we could so as to prevent us from all being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was Mr. Edin Novalic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was he the commander of that particular detachment, that is to say, that whole group of people who were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was no detachment. It was nothing organised. We weren't under any orders. We had just quite simply gathered there in order to try to survive as best we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I think that I can say this in a public session because I think he was a witness testifying in public session in the Aleksovski trial. The witness I mentioned a moment ago, Mr. Novalic, said that asked by the Prosecution, you answered that you were, for the most part, armed with snipers and grenades. That is page 437 of the transcript from the Aleksovski trial, and I'll tell you the date. It is the 23rd of February, 1998. So snipers and grenades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is what another witness said in another trial; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, the witness who was in Mahala/Strana and described the evening that we're talking about, Edin Novalic, and the witness has just agreed his name was Edin Novalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. J, is there anything you want to say about that or not? You're being asked to comment on what apparently some other witness said in another trial, not in this trial. If you've got nothing to say about it, just say "No."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what he said. I know what the situation was and what we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that several people were killed. I have the names, but I don't want to read them out now. But we know how they were killed, before the fighting had ceased, that is to say, there was some fighting because a part of the soldiers tried to move along the bed of the Ivancica River and to avoid being captured, so some succeeded in escaping and others were killed in the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean it didn't happen like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any duty to perform? Were you the commander of a platoon or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, nobody had any assignments, nobody did any commanding. We all discussed amongst ourselves what was to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me try and follow the instructions from the Judges and move on more rapidly. I'm going to try and move through the next set of questions as quickly as possible. In looking at the transcript from yesterday's testimony, I don't think you answered one of my questions when I asked you why you were imprisoned in the silo as a soldier of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, because I didn't turn up for two shifts, and I was punished for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So for discipline? Lack of discipline, that is to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, were disciplinary measures taken against you previously? I mean before the war, any sanctions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not in court, I had no dealings of that kind, as far as I know, only something that might have happened in the course of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were disciplined in your company twice, related to some prices, prices of Cognac or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's my private affair.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You say your private affair. Very well. I have another piece of information that in 1991, for example, that you were tried at the Basic Court in Zenica, and I tried to check this out. I think it had something to do with security, traffic security, Article 181, para 3, of the law of Bosnia-Herzegovina; you were prosecuted on the basis of that Article. Did you have any traffic accidents or anything like that in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know what that could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: On the 13th of August --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're not putting it to him that he was convicted of a traffic offence, are you, in relation to his credibility here?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) No, Your Honour. I just wanted to see whether my interpretation of the article was true and exact and whether the article referred to traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, before we go on, let me just understand. What is the offence that you're suggesting that he was prosecuted for?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I think that it was a traffic offence, but I wasn't quite sure, and that's why I asked the witness. If it did relate to traffic, I have no more questions, but the witness doesn't seem to recall the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't sound as though it's very important. Yes, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I think, after all, Mr. Naumovski, that you should avoid this type of question if you're not sure. You are talking about a traffic accident. I must draw your attention to the fact that you have to avoid a waste of time for yourself and the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that you saw HV and HVO insignia on some soldiers, that some of them had "HV" and some of them had "HVO", that is to say, January of 1993, the 25th of January, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 25th of January, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were there many soldiers with these HV insignias?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you the exact number, but there were far less -- I saw only two or three insignias. At that point, I only saw that. The others had HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you talk to any of those young men who had the HV patches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we were fighting for survival. We didn't talk to anybody. We had to place our heads down on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, those you mentioned in the brigades, did they have two types of patches or one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I just read the Vunolist (phoen) insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, asked by the Prosecutor, you said that whenever something occurred in Busovaca, other military units of the HVO would come from Vitez, Kiseljak, Travnik, and so on. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, in January and the events of the 25th of January, were there any units from Kiseljak, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that, sir, but I do know that they came from Vitez because they guarded me in Putis. And that they had come from all parts, I also know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I'm talking about the 25th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were a lot of unknown individuals in uniform. For us, they were people we did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, let us just touch upon some of the names that you mentioned yesterday, answering questions from the Prosecutor. Mitko Cosic, for example. The Prosecutor used a term which I don't think was appropriate, so please help me. He said that it was an intervention platoon, prisoners' intervention platoon. It was just called an intervention platoon, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that you knew nothing of whether Mr. Cosic had any dealings with Mr. Kordic, but you say that you do know that he went along the road to Tisovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What period are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, before the 20th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Mitko Cosic has a family in the village of Ravan, anybody he's related to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, quite possibly he does have. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it is possible that he was visiting somebody in the village of Ravan and not going to visit Mr. Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's a bit of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You still maintain that he was going to see Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: As a conclusion, that's your conclusion; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the other person was Vlado Cosic. As far as I know, he is not Mitko Cosic's brother.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he is a cousin on his father's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he was a policeman in ex-Yugoslavia and that he stayed on in those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But in January 1993 in Busovaca, do you know what function he had there then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. In January, I really can't say. All I know is that he was a policeman, and he was no ordinary policeman either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who his chief was, commander in military terms, along the military chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember any names, sir, now; I really can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the so-called 4th Battalion of the military police in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. One of the names that we talked about was Gavro Maric, a man working as a clerk in the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, at least I think he performed that kind of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I agree with you. But you said, about that particular man, that he was the commander of Kordic's units, and you used the plural. Which units, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't really know. I don't dare say exactly, because I'm not quite sure. But as I said, he was an officer of some kind and he was one of the commanders, I think he was, but the name doesn't say much, doesn't tell me much, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, it doesn't say much to me either. But you said that he was one of Kordic's commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But he was not my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about the man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. The next name is Mr. Nikica Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the chief of the civilian police in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and we went to school together. I know all about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that he was president of the commission for exchange? You know that these exchange commissions existed on both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, probably they did, and probably he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I'm asking you this because when you spoke about him the last time, you did not say that he was a member of the commission for exchange but coordinator for transfer, but you had in mind this particular post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he would transfer everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did the Muslim side have this type of commission and their man who negotiated with Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you a great deal about Mr. Anto Sliskovic, and I'm going to ask you about that in the shortest possible terms. Do you know what his duties were, what function he performed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know he was a SIS man, as we popularly used to call it, and that he was the number-one man after Kordic, that he was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said he was a SIS man. For what territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, for Busovaca, and I'm generally speaking about the Busovaca area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Anto Sliskovic was the assistant to the commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, that is to say, Colonel Blaskic's forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone were, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not interested in any of that. I never was interested in any of it. What I'm interested in was Anto Sliskovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- because he was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Anto Sliskovic carried out all orders from Mr. Kordic into effect. I took note of that. I have to keep repeating the same question. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he had some orders that he had to carry out, and in fact he carried out Kordic's orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How much longer are you going to be now, Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
